679: The Vibram Solace (Super Overstable Lace) is the ultra overstable distance driver in the Vibram Line. Vibram says this about the Solace: “Our most overstable disc to date, this disc can handle all the power you give it, will consistently fight any headwind you throw it at, and will have a predictable (and big) fade at the end of its flight. When you are ready to be in control, reach for the Solace” Like the Lace, the Vibram Solace is a wide rimmed distance driver with a 2.4cm wing. This disc has the same diameter and rim depth, but is slightly thinner than the popular Lace.
684: Vibram’s Notch is the company’s first truly overstable fairway, PDGA-approved on April 20, 2015, built to fight wind and finish with a confident, heavy fade. The comfortable, modest rim pairs with grippy X-Link rubber so releases feel consistent, tree hits kick less, and ground play stays minimal—money in the woods. Players lean on it for forehand control, forced hyzers, and headwind tee shots; powered down it becomes a point-and-dump placement tool you can trust. It arrived with Vibram’s 2015 fairway wave alongside the Arch and Valley and appeared in Firm, Medium, Soft, plus occasional Glow and “Granite” chunk blends. Vibram’s 2018 exit makes the Notch out of regular production today, which is why loyal throwers guard theirs like gold.
689: The O-Lace is Vibrams flagship distance driver, offering consistant overstability without being too beefy. The O-Lace has much more consistancy than the Lace (it's flippy counterpart)
696: The Prodigy F Model S is a stable fairway driver introduced in 2020 as part of Prodigys Ace Line, designed to offer a balance of speed and control for players of various skill levels. With its comfortable rim and consistent flight path, the F Model S excels at hyzer flips, straight shots, and gentle turnovers, making it a versatile choice for navigating tight fairways and executing precise lines. Its design allows for a reliable finish, providing confidence in both backhand and forehand throws. The F Model S serves as a dependable workhorse in a players bag, bridging the gap between fairway and distance drivers.
700: The PD3 is Discmania’s most overstable distance driver, built for extreme wind, skip shots, and power forehands. It was released as a limited fundraiser for the 2020 European Open and is now out of production. With its flat top and sharp fade, it’s a favorite among big-arm throwers who need a disc that won’t back down.
701: The Discraft Wildcat is a discontinued distance driver that once offered a balanced blend of speed, glide, and control. Known for its low-profile design and manageable rim, it was favored by players seeking a disc that could handle both backhand and forehand throws with ease. While it may no longer be in production, the Wildcat remains a cherished find for collectors and those who appreciated its reliable flight characteristics.
702: The MVP Motion is MVP’s most overstable distance driver—a wind-defying utility beast built to resist turnover and finish with authority. Since its 2014 debut, it’s been MVP’s go-to for headwind hucks, torque-resistant forehands, and bulletproof placement drives using their signature GYRO® tech. Reviewers compare it to a beefier Resistor or Axiom Fireball, praising its straight, fade-heavy flight even with power throwers. One player dubbed it “a distance driver that handles like a fairway driver,” thanks to its modest grip and dependable fade. If your bag needs a rock-solid, windproof workhorse, the Motion earns its name—and your trust.
706: The Sergeant is Dynamic Discs’ hybrid-style distance driver, bridging the gap between fairway and high-speed drivers. It offers a comfortable rim for both backhand and forehand throws, providing a reliable fade without being overly aggressive. Ideal for shots that require more distance than a fairway driver but less power than a full-speed driver, the Sergeant delivers consistent performance for intermediate to advanced players.
707: RPMs Kotare is the overstable workhorse distance driver of their lineup. If you need consistant and hard fade at the end of a distance flight, or need a disc good in headwinds, the Kotare is your bird.
708: The Innova Invictus is a speed 10 overstable distance driver introduced in early 2020. Designed for power throwers, it excels in headwinds and offers a reliable fade, making it ideal for long-range forehands, extreme hyzer throws, and force-over flex lines. Garrett Gurthie, a member of Innova's Star Team, has referred to the Invictus as a "faster Firebird," highlighting its utility for those with significant arm speed.
711: The Discraft Hades is an understable distance driver introduced as part of Paul McBeth’s signature lineup. It offers a high-speed profile with significant glide, making it ideal for long, controlled drives. The Hades is designed to provide easy turnovers and long, graceful flights, catering to players seeking maximum distance with less effort. With a flight rating of Speed 12, Glide 6, Turn -3, and Fade 2, the Hades is suitable for intermediate to advanced players. Its understable nature allows for hyzer flips and long anhyzers, while still offering a reliable fade at the end of its flight. The Hades is available in various plastic blends, including ESP and Big Z, each providing different grip and durability characteristics. The ESP plastic offers a tacky grip and consistent performance in various weather conditions, while the Big Z plastic provides a durable, slightly flexible feel with vibrant designs. Overall, the Discraft Hades is a versatile distance driver that combines speed, glide, and understability, making it a valuable addition to many disc golf bags.
712: The Legacy Vengeance is a speed 10 control driver introduced in 2020, designed to bridge the gap between fairway and distance drivers. With a flat profile and comfortable rim, it offers a stable-to-overstable flight, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. The Vengeance provides a reliable fade, allowing for controlled distance shots and versatility in various playing conditions. Originally released as a Drew Gibson signature disc, the Vengeance has been praised for its performance and feel. Players have noted its ability to handle power while maintaining control, making it a valuable addition to many disc golf bags. The disc's design allows for a straight flight with a dependable finish, catering to players seeking consistency and precision. In terms of comparisons, the Vengeance is often likened to a longer Rival with added speed and stability, fitting seamlessly into Legacy's lineup. Its flight characteristics make it a versatile option for players looking to expand their range without sacrificing control.
713: The Kastaplast Lots , introduced around 2020, is a neutral-to-stable fairway driver designed for precision and predictability. Its name means "pilot" in Swedish—apt for a disc that reliably steers straight through tight fairways. With gentle turn and firm fade, it holds whatever line you put it on—especially when thrown flat. Players love the premium K1 plastic for its grip and durability, noting it delivers surprising distance for a stable fairway mold. Compared to deep-rimmed fairways like the Falk, the Lots offers a sleeker profile, smoother glide, and more workability, making it an excellent choice for technical placement shots or controlled flex lines.
716: The Mint Discs Alpha is a power fairway driver built for straight, reliable distance and a dependable fade. It consistently holds its line—resisting high-speed turn—before finishing clean, making it great for tight tunnels, headwind throwers, and placement-focused shots. While sturdy enough to handle aggressive power, it remains accessible to intermediate players thanks to its predictable flight. Over successive runs, the Alpha has flattened its dome and lost some high-speed stability, making newer runs easier to throw crisply. Many players compare its feel and flight to a slightly more stable Teebird, swapping between the two without loss of precision. Whether you're attacking technical lines or need a reliable workhorse driver, the Alpha delivers power, precision, and consistency that holds up over time.
718: The Mint Discs Freetail is a glide-happy understable driver that turns with ease and doesn’t ask much of your arm. It’s perfect for players learning to shape long turnover lines or execute smooth hyzer-flips that stay in the air forever. Intermediate and advanced throwers love it for powered-down rollers or tailwind bombs that drift gracefully. The rim is comfortably shaped, giving you the confidence to hit tight gaps or stretch open fairways. Like its namesake bat from Austin, the Freetail is all about graceful movement through the sky—just don’t expect it to fade back home if you overpower it.
719: The D Model OS is an overstable distance driver that is power player's dream. Those with more power can throw this disc hard, and it will work to fight out of its slight high-speed turn and finish with a harder fade, thanks to its fast, overstable flight. D Model discs are built for maximum distance and have a sharp nose and slight dome for increased speed and glide. They also feature medium-depth rim to allow a comfortable grip across different hand sizes.
723: The Discmania Essence is a fairway driver that falls on the understable side—a perfect companion for players building power or dialing precision. It offers smooth turnovers and reliable glide, making it ideal for hyzer flips, rollers, and shape shots without demanding torque. Its rounded, semi-blunt nose gives it a confident feel in hand and excellent roller potential. Loved by beginners and still trusted by seasoned throwers, the Essence excels at making tight lines and technical setups more approachable on any course.
725: The Latitude 64 Sapphire is a lightweight distance driver designed for easy speed and big glide. Part of the Easy-to-Use line, it helps developing players unlock max distance with less effort. Expect gentle turn, a touch of fade, and smooth hyzer-flips—even at lower arm speeds. Great for newer players or those looking for effortless distance without overpowering the throw.
727: The Millennium Polaris LF , PDGA-approved in 1996, is a vintage yet remarkable fairway driver known for its unique combo of extreme dome, high glide, and surprisingly reliable fade. Despite its Speed 9 rating, the Polaris LF behaves more like a distance driver, excelling in hyzer flips, flex shots, and even tailwind bombing. Reviewers from its 90s run note it’s “stupidly domey and glidey” yet resists turn in wind—an almost mythical pairing for early discs . Though out-of-production, its rare runs are prized for offering a floaty, high-flying ride with a dependable finish—perfect for collectors or throwers chasing retro flair.
728: The Crush is a discontinued overstable distance driver from Discraft, designed for power throwers seeking a reliable fade. With a speed rating of 11 and a fade of 4, it excels in headwinds and forehand throws, offering a consistent flight path. While no longer in regular production, the Crush remains a sought-after disc for advanced players looking for dependable overstability.
729: The MVP Impulse is a smooth, understable distance driver that thrives on hyzer-flips and long turnover flights. With forgiving glide and reliable fade, it’s ideal for players refining form or needing shape control over pure power. It resists wobble, holds flat to mild anhyzer lines, and finishes clean—whether you're driving backhand or turning over with forehands. Many find it the easiest disc to consistently hyzer-flip and trust through narrow fairways or tailwind bombing. Compared to its stable siblings like the Inertia or Virus, the Impulse leans more understable and offers smoother, more controllable turnover potential without sacrificing accuracy. For beginners & intermediates, it's often the go-to driver for adding distance and confidence. For advanced players, it fills a gap in the bag for shaping touch shots, rollers, and finesse flights when something just a bit more workable is needed.
741: The Mentor is a versatile 11-speed distance driver from Discmanias Active lineup, designed to offer controlled distance with a touch of understability. Its flight characteristics make it suitable for players seeking a disc that can handle both power and finesse. With a comfortable rim and consistent flight, the Mentor is a reliable choice for shaping various shot types.
744: The MVP Inertia is a controllable distance driver loved for its blend of glide, turn, and fade—offering a smooth hyzer-flip for power throwers and straight, dependable flights for those with moderate arm strength. It resists wobble and holds flat or slight anhyzer lines before delivering a clean finish, making it ideal for accuracy-focused big throws. Many players report it flies straighter than comparable molds and carves long S-curves with ease. It’s often compared to more understable fairways as a straighter, more dependable option that still locks in a predictable fade. The Inertia shines on hyzer-flip distance drives, tailwind bomb shots, and placement drives that need reliable carry without overshooting. It’s a trustworthy go-to when you want distance with control—not a flashy bomb, but a dependable workhorse.
747: The Longhorn is Mint Discs’ stable-to-overstable distance driver, designed to complement the understable Freetail. With a speed rating of 11, it offers a slight high-speed turn followed by a dependable fade, making it suitable for hyzer flips, controlled distance shots, and moderate wind conditions. Its flight characteristics place it between a Wraith and a Destroyer, providing a balance of control and power for players seeking reliable performance.
755: The Millennium Draco is a flat-topped, overstable distance driver built for precision, power, and wind-defying confidence. Launched in 2019 and made by Innova for Millennium, it blends Firebird DNA with a reinforced shoulder for added torque resistance—think of it as a Firebird on steroids. Ideal for hyzer shots, skip placement, and headwind hammering, it rewards hard throws with consistent finishes. One forum user said, “The Draco likes to be thrown really hard, and will reward you with good, flat flights and decent distance.” Another described it as a “beastly utility driver for 250+-foot rollers and flex lines.” It’s your go-to when you need reliable flight under fire.
759: The Barbarian is a trustworthy fairway driver built for balance and control. It holds straight lines with confidence before finishing with a gentle, dependable fade. Its flight feels instinctive — you can throw it hard without fear of turning it over, yet it won’t fight out too early. Players often lean on the Barbarian when they need a single disc that can handle most fairway duties, from controlled tee shots to placement drives in windy woods. It’s not flashy, but it’s one of those molds that quietly earns its place through sheer reliability.
760: The Prodigy F Model US is a versatile fairway driver from Prodigy’s Ace Line, designed to offer controllable understability for players of all skill levels. With a straight flight and a consistent late turn, the F Model US excels at hyzer flips, long anhyzers, and gentle turnovers. It has more glide than many Prodigy molds and fills the gap between beginner-friendly drivers and seasoned turnover tools. While it’s not part of the main numbered Prodigy lineup, the F Model US helped establish the Ace Line as a budget-friendly but capable option in the Prodigy ecosystem.
761: The Prodigy Ace Line F Model OS is an overstable fairway driver introduced in 2020, designed for players seeking a reliable and consistent flight path. With its pronounced fade and moderate glide, it excels in headwinds, force-over flex shots, and forehand throws. The disc's design allows it to stand up to flat when thrown hard, providing a dependable finish at the end of its flight. Its tendency to skip upon landing adds utility in shot-making scenarios. The F Model OS is suitable for players of various skill levels, offering a balance between control and distance.
783: The Gateway Spear is a Speed 9 control driver designed for clean releases, long glide, and straight flights with a touch of finesse. Approved in 2019, it’s one of Gateway’s most accessible and versatile drivers—ideal for hyzer-flips, gentle turnovers, or line-holding lasers down narrow fairways. It has a slightly domey profile and a comfortable rim that works well for both forehand and backhand throws. As it beats in, the Spear becomes even more workable without becoming touchy. If you’re looking for a fairway driver that blends distance with pinpoint accuracy, the Spear hits the mark with confidence.
789: The Discraft Flash was a slightly understable distance driver released in the early 2000s and made famous by its surprising speed and glide. Known for effortless distance with just a touch of turn and reliable fade, it catered to intermediate players and power throwers alike. The Flash was one of Discraft’s earlier attempts to compete with high-speed drivers from other brands and even saw PDGA Worlds success, with Nate Doss throwing it en route to his 2005 title. Though now out of production, the Flash still lives on in collectors' bags and old-school throwers who swear by its balanced, workable flight.
791: The Majesty is part of Discmania's Active Line, made by Yikun Discs in China. It has a wide rim, allowing it to fly very fast and with a lot of glide.
799: Dynamic Discs’ Evader is a modern “do-everything” control fairway built to give Escape throwers a sturdier, wind-friendlier option without jumping all the way to a Felon. Typically a touch flatter with tempered glide, it shrugs off torque, tracks forward on a line, then finishes with that clean, reliable fade you can lean on for placement golf. Backhand or forehand, it excels at force-hyzers, powered-down fairway chips, and headwind tee shots that still need distance control rather than a dump. Players often slot it between the Escape and Getaway, with special runs (think firmer tour blends or the premium Supreme feel) nudging stability up a notch. If you like “point and commit,” the Evader rarely argues.
800: The Lace, Long Distance Driver: Find the extra distance you’ve been looking for with The Lace, Vibram’s long distance driver. Stability and range allow this disc to go further, while high-grip technology helps maintain grip and accuracy, even in wet conditions.
802: The Vibram Onyx is a straight-flying fairway driver known for its consistency and comfortable feel. It offers reliable control with minimal fade, making it useful for shaping lines and navigating tight fairways. Like all Vibram discs, it features a unique rubber blend that provides excellent grip and a soft, durable flight plate. The Onyx is no longer in production following Vibram’s exit from disc golf in 2018, but it remains a sought-after option for players who value control, grip, and a smooth, neutral flight.
804: The Innova Starfire L—also known as the SL—is a control-oriented distance driver offering a straighter, more glide-focused flight than the standard Starfire. With a touch of turn and a reliable fade, it excels at long hyzer-flips, extended turnovers, and precision drives that demand finesse over brute force. Though now out of regular production, the Starfire L remains a sought-after mold for players seeking a balanced driver that bridges the gap between fairway control and distance potential.
805: The RPM Discs Kiwi is a dependable overstable distance driver, retooled and approved by the PDGA in April 2020. Designed to handle a variety of wind conditions, it offers a consistent fade, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. The Kiwis flight characteristics provide a reliable option for players seeking control and stability in their distance shots.
823: The Infinite Discs Aztec is a speed 10 distance driver that offers a straight flight with a gentle fade, providing surprising distance and accuracy for a disc in its class. Its narrower rim enhances comfort and control, making it accessible to a wide range of players. The Aztec is often compared to longer versions of the Exodus or Dynasty, delivering familiar control with added range. Whether you're executing controlled fairway drives or seeking reliable placement shots, the Aztec's performance makes it a valuable addition to any disc golfer's bag.
824: The Emperor is a high-speed distance driver with glide, turn, and a reliably strong finish—ideal for max-distance shots with controlled fade. If you miss the original Discmania DD3 from the Innova days, the Emperor is essentially that mold reborn. Power throwers will love its stability, while intermediate players can count on its consistent fade for long flex lines and windy throws.
825: The Infinite Discs Scepter is a flat-top, ultra-overstable fairway driver crafted for raw power and precision. Approved in 2019, it was built as Infinite’s response to the stability of a Firebird, but with a flatter profile for bulletproof forehand grip and consistency. It slices through headwinds, resists anhyzer releases, and finishes with a sharp, dependable fade—ideal for spike hyzers, forehands, and placement drives. Power throwers appreciate how it handles torque with ease, while controlled rollers enjoy its flat top and hard finish. If you're seeking a no-nonsense utility disc that refuses to bend under stress, the Scepter reigns supreme.
826: The Infinite Sphinx is a glide-rich, understable fairway driver that shines for players at all levels. Beginners will love how it hyzer-flips easily and covers maximum distance before smoothly fading, while seasoned throwers tap into its potential for hyzer-flips, long turnovers, and low rollers. Its forgiving yet stable flight resists unwanted wobble, even when thrown flat. Wingspan and profile combine to create a predictable, tunnel-capable line that’s both fun and functional. Flight characteristics often mirror molds like Sidewinder or Roadrunner, offering familiarity to those transitioning. Plastics vary slightly in initial stability, but I‑Blend runs quickly become dependable flippers. Versatile, approachable, and trusting without drama—the Sphinx earns a spot in bags looking for both utility and confidence.
827: In case you didn't know, all of Infinite's discs are made by Innova. Most molds are tweaked Innova discs, or mixed tops and bottoms of Innova molds. The Slab is very similar to Innova's Max, a very overstable disc, meant for utility shots more than workhorse driving.
829: The Exodus was Infinite Discs’ first true driver release, and it’s widely acknowledged that the disc is manufactured by Innova. Reviews and user comparisons often point to it being an Eagle L clone — its top feels close to the Gazelle, its bottom rim recalls the TeeBird L. It flies as a stable, straight-to-finish fairway driver: it resists flip under power but gives you clean, consistent fade. Because of its Innova-derived skeleton, it slots naturally near the middle of Innova’s fairway range — it behaves like a more neutral Eagle or even lighter Teebird, rather than pushing into overstable territory. Many players use it as their “Innova-feel, but slightly fresher mold” driver choice, especially on wooded or midrange-length holes.
832: The Pharaoh is basicaly Infinite's version of the Innova Shryke. It's definitely not exactly the same, but it's very similar.
835: The Grand Rive is a high-speed distance driver that offers the perfect combination of power and precision. With its overstable flight path and exceptional glide, the Rive is built for players who need control and distance in all conditions. Whether youre battling headwinds or aiming for powerful fades, the Rive delivers consistent, reliable results. Trusted by 2x World Champion Isaac Robinson, it’s a disc built to perform at the highest level.
839: The DGA Hypercane is a fast and very overstable distance driver with great glide and significant fade. The Hypercane has the stability you can count on in the windiest of conditions!
841: The Pulse is an overstable distance driver with a unique groove top, offering a comfortable grip for forehand throws. Designed for power throwers, it delivers consistent fade and excels in windy conditions. Comparable to the Innova Orc or MVP Tesla, the Pulse provides reliable performance for players seeking a dependable forehand driver.
842: The original Discraft Venom, approved by the PDGA in 2005, was a speed 12 overstable distance driver with a narrow 2.2 cm rim. Primarily produced in Pro D plastic, it also saw limited runs in ESP and Z plastics. Known for its unique flight, it exhibited a slight high-speed turn followed by a strong, late fade, making it a favorite for overhand throws, forehands, and headwind shots. Despite its niche appeal, it was discontinued around 2010 due to limited demand. In 2023, Discraft reintroduced the Venom as a retooled, more overstable mold, distinct from the original. Collectors and enthusiasts still seek out the original for its distinctive flight characteristics.
843: The Discraft Talon is a highly overstable fairway driver known for its pinpoint control and strong, reliable fade. Released in the mid-2000s and later discontinued, it built a cult following thanks to its ability to hold torque-heavy lines without turning over. It excels in windy conditions, tight fairways, and utility shots like forehands, overhands, and low skip hyzers. The Talon features a comfortable, beadless rim and a flat profile that feels clean on both backhand and forehand grips. Though it was never a distance bomber, its power lies in predictability—offering a straight push with a hard finish that makes it a dependable choice when placement is critical. Even years after its discontinuation, the Talon remains a favorite for players who value consistent, overstable performance.
849: The Astronaut is a fast, understable distance driver designed for players seeking maximum distance with minimal effort. Its high speed and significant turn make it ideal for hyzer flips, long anhyzers, and even roller shots. While it's accessible for newer players aiming to achieve longer drives, those with higher arm speeds may find it excels as a controlled roller or for shaping specific lines. Note that stability can vary between runs, so it's advisable to test individual discs for consistency.
850: The Discmania Rockstar is an understable fairway driver originally released as part of the Active line, which was molded in China and later discontinued. Designed with newer players in mind, it offers effortless glide and a controllable turn, making it ideal for hyzer flips, turnovers, and shaping technical lines. The rounded rim and shallow profile provide a comfortable grip and smooth release. Though no longer in regular production, the Rockstar still stands out as a workable option for players seeking easy distance with minimal effort.
854: The Fu is a control driver designed to stay on line, even when thrown with power. It offers a neutral-to-stable flight that favors precision over aggression, making it ideal for shaping straight or gently fading fairway shots. Where many fairway drivers require constant touch adjustments, the Fu rewards confident, clean releases and resists unexpected turn. It excels on tight, technical courses and rewards repeatable form. Once you’ve learned its lines, it becomes the kind of disc you trust to go exactly where you aim.
857: The Ragnarok is Viking Discs’ stable distance driver, designed for long control shots with tight S-curves and reliable fades. With flight numbers of 11/5/-1/2, it offers a comfortable rim and is suitable for players of all skill levels. Depending on your release angle, the Ragnarok can be useful in various situations, providing versatility and consistent performance.
858: The Grace is Kristin Lätt’s signature distance driver—built for smooth speed, glide, and shot shaping. Its like a Wraith with a bit more finesse, perfect for backhand bombs and confident forehands alike. If it’s good enough for a world champ, it’s worth a spot in your bag.
864: The Prodigy H4 V2 is an understable hybrid driver that blends fairway precision with extra distance potential. As part of the retooled H Series, the V2 version featured a flatter top, improved grip, and more glide than the original H4. Designed for long turnovers, hyzer flips, and controlled shots through the woods, it’s especially useful for players with moderate arm speed looking to stretch their drives without sacrificing control. The H4 V2 helped refine Prodigys hybrid lineup, offering a sweet spot between the flippier H5 and the more stable H3 V2.
867: The Scorch is Discraft’s answer to effortless distance—an 11-speed with high glide, gentle turn, and a dependable finish. It’s great for hyzer flips, long anhyzers, or tailwind drives, especially for intermediate players looking to stretch their range without overpowering their shot.
874: The RPM Pekapeka is an understable fairway driver built for effortless shaping and controlled glide. It excels at hyzer-flips, long turnover shots, and rollers, making it especially useful in wooded fairways or technical approaches. Despite being a 9-speed, it feels surprisingly workable and neutral in flight, with a smooth turn that holds without diving. Many players compare it favorably to molds like the Sidewinder but find the Pekapeka offers more control and a touch more finesse. It’s well-loved for its consistency across different plastics and its ability to handle both forehand and backhand lines with equal reliability. Whether you’re an experienced thrower carving tight lines or a newer player looking for easy distance, the Pekapeka is a reliable, glide-heavy tool that brings quiet confidence to the bag.
877: The Curl is Lone Star’s go-to understable distance driver, designed for easy distance with minimal effort. With a smooth high-speed turn and moderate fade, it’s ideal for controlled S-curves, long turnovers, or tailwind bombs. Intermediate players will find it accessible, while power throwers can use it for finesse distance shots. It slots neatly below faster Lone Star drivers like the Warbird, offering a manageable rim and a consistent, workable flight.
878: The Lone Star Discs Mad Cat debuted around late 2020 as a slim, speed‑9 overstable fairway driver designed for power throwers and wind mastery. Its low-profile, flat shape excels in torque-heavy forehands, hyzer bombs, and headwind drives, delivering a sharp, predictable fade. Players note its premium feel—with firm yet touchable plastic—and versatility across backhand and forehand grips. Compared to wider-rimmed fairways, the Mad Cat feels more controlled and less drift-prone, making it a favorite for pin-point placement. If you’re after a refined, wind-busting utility driver that fits tight lines and fights the breeze, the Mad Cat deserves a spot in your bag.
879: The Discraft Reaper is a deliberate, overstable fairway driver that thrives where precision meets wind. It’s built for sweeping hyzer shots and tight placement drives—often outlasting competitors during strong headwinds or off-angle throws. While once discontinued, it has made sporadic comebacks in limited runs, keeping its cult following alive. Players appreciate its control—clean hyzers hold true until a firm fade arrives, rarely surprising with late-turn or skips thanks to its balanced stability. Though slower in speed than modern molds, it’s often favored for minimizing tree skips and delivering confidence on every throw. The Reaper doesn’t chase distance; it demands intent, rewarding players with predictable, hyzer-locked finishes that make it a go-to when accuracy is paramount and wind resistance is crucial.
883: No, not David. Like the knife. The Bowie rounds out the Lone Star overstable 13-speed collection. Its the flippiest of the four (Tombstone, Sequin, Crocket), but still isnt that flippy.
885: The Discraft Passion is a signature fairway driver designed in collaboration with Paige Pierce, built for straight, glidey flights with minimal fade. It features a flat top and a comfortable rim shape that appeals to players who prefer clean releases and precise control. Originally inspired by the feel and flight of the Cyclone, the Passion is especially useful for shaping tight lines and executing touch shots with confidence. Whether thrown on hyzer, flat, or slight anhyzer, it tends to hold the angle and stay on track, making it a reliable option for controlled drives at a variety of power levels
893: The Adder is ready to bail disc golfers out of the windiest of conditions. With high speed and a pop top giving good glide, only the biggest arms will have a chance to make this disc turn over. For everyone else, it will be a very useable utility disc for when you need a distinct fade with speed through the flightpath.
900: From Daredevil Discs: Holding the ‘Flex Performance’ plastic distance driver in your hand, or watching it fly down the fairway, you may be convinced there’s wizardry in play. This swift and fierce flier in the wind, is designed for big distance. The fine-tuned turn of the Merlin allows for breakneck maneuvers around any obstacle on the course. Great for cold weather play and dyes very well.
904: The Viking Discs Fenrir is a 10-speed overstable distance driver introduced in late 2020. Designed for power throwers, it offers a reliable flight path with a consistent fade, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. The Fenrirs design allows it to hold hyzer lines effectively, even in windy conditions. Its flight characteristics are comparable to discs like the Innova Invictus or Westside Fortress, providing a dependable option for players seeking control and stability in their distance shots.
910: The Crosslap Vigil is an approachable fairway driver with an understable bias, tailored especially for players just starting out. It features smooth, glidey flight and a clean release, making it effortless to roll into hyzer-flip-to-straight lines or smooth S-curves. It’s the kind of disc that stays true to the line you feed it, offering reliability and predictability—perfect for learning control or shaping precise fairway paths.
912: The Odin is Viking Discs’ answer to power distance, offering a familiar profile and flight reminiscent of the Destroyer or DD3. It’s a dependable choice for experienced players looking for long, controllable flights with a reliable fade. Whether you’re ripping forehands or backhands, the Odin holds up to torque and performs well in headwinds. Great for those who want high-speed distance without sacrificing control.
915: The MVP Wave is a versatile distance driver known for its controllable understability and impressive glide. Ideal for hyzer flips, long turnovers, and tailwind drives, it offers a smooth, S-shaped flight path that suits a variety of skill levels. Advanced players will appreciate its capacity for shaping precise lines, while intermediate throwers can rely on its forgiveness and distance potential. The Wave's design allows it to adapt to different throwing styles, making it a valuable addition to many disc golf bags.
916: The MVP Phase is a power thrower’s dream: a flat-topped, overstable distance driver that thrives in headwinds and handles torque like a champ. It’s the beefiest member of MVP’s 21.5mm distance class, offering a reliable fade and minimal turn. If you’re looking for a disc that won’t flinch under pressure—forehand or backhand—the Phase delivers.
919: The Thought Space Athletics Mantra is a smooth, glide-focused understable fairway driver crafted for control and shaping power. Often considered a beefed-up Wing speed above typical fairways, it delivers long hyzer-flips, clean turnovers, and controllable rollers with ease. Players report it holds straight lines even into tailwinds and remains dependable when thrown flat—making it exceptional for precision placement. It’s also surprisingly durable yet still flexible enough to work on aesthetic plastics that season into more turnover-friendly flyers. The Mantra feels slightly faster than a traditional 9-speed, closer to a manageable 10-speed, while avoiding overpowering stability. It’s the archetype of a versatile control driver: user-friendly for newer players, yet offering enough glide and finesse to earn a place in advanced bags.
923: The MVP Orbital is the most understable driver in MVP’s 21.5mm distance class, designed for players seeking maximum turn and glide. Ideal for hyzer flips, long turnovers, and rollers, it caters to those with lower arm speeds aiming for extended flights. Power throwers can exploit its understability for creative shot shapes and finesse lines. Introduced in 2015, the Orbital offers a unique flight experience within MVP's lineup.
925: The Axiom Vanish is an understable distance driver that offers a controllable, glidey flight. It excels at hyzer flips and long turnovers, making it suitable for players seeking easy distance with manageable stability. The Vanish's comfortable rim and consistent flight path make it a reliable choice for various shot shapes and conditions.
929: The Innova FL (Firebird‑L) was introduced in 2007 as a less aggressive sibling to the Firebird. Designed with a straighter, more glide-friendly flight, the FL maintains the torque resistance players love, but with a longer, more workable finish. It’s a go-to for players who want Firebird-like dependability without the early, hard fade—especially useful for long forehands, wind control, and controlled S-curves. The rim feels familiar, but the flight offers just enough finesse to carve cleaner lines. If you’ve ever wished your Firebird would stay straight just a bit longer, the FL fills that gap perfectly.
930: The Cedar is AGL’s flagship overstable distance driver, crafted to replace the retired Cypress. With a shallow rim and reliable fade, it excels in headwinds and power forehands. Flight-wise, it’s reminiscent of the out-of-production Innova TeeRex, offering a dependable finish for big arms.
932: Sycamore is AGL’s attempt to deliver a neutral-plus fairway driver that players can trust for clean lines. It came out at a time when AGL was expanding beyond utility and putter molds, aiming to produce full roads with controlled shapes. Its flight leans straight with a subtle fade, ideal for shaping forehands or carving backhand fades when needed. Because it doesn’t force its will on you, it’s often used as a shaping tool in wooded or technical courses, where you want to control finish more than push speed.
941: The Discraft Captain’s Raptor is the mightiest, most overstable fairway driver Discraft makes—crafted in collaboration with Paul Ulibarri to push durability and reliability to their limits. It’s built for spike hyzers, torque-resistant forehands, and no-compromise placement drives. Since its debut, it's been hailed as the go-to wind warrior for players who demand precision. One Redditor noted it's “much more overstable than any Firebird I’ve thrown,” while another called it an “overstable scramble machine” perfect for 250–300 ft flex shots. Limited-release and once-a-year runs make it exclusive, but if you need a disc that won’t bend, the Captain’s Raptor is your anchor.
943: The Max is Innova’s ultra-overstable distance driver, built for power throwers and extreme conditions. It’s a go-to for headwinds, flex lines, and forehand bombs that demand a hard, reliable finish. Think of it as a faster Firebird or a more aggressive Monster—just don’t expect it to glide for days. Now out of production, but still a favorite among those who like their discs beefy and predictable.
946: The MVP Terra is a confidently overstable fairway driver built for wind, forehand power, and precise placement. Designed by James Conrad, it offers a straight-to-fade flight that resists high-speed turn and holds reliable hyzer lines even into stiff headwinds. Players appreciate its consistent fade—it glides while maintaining forward momentum before finishing with a smooth pan-type fade. It’s often described as a less aggressive but more glidey version of traditional overstable molds like Firebird or Thunderbird, with plenty of torque resistance and control. Both backhand and forehand throwers value its grip and predictability. Whether you're lining up tight fairways, battling wind, or seeking a reliable forehand workhorse, the Terra excels. It's built to resist surprises and deliver confidence—no matter the wind or angle.
948: From Prodigy: The Reverb is our collaboration with Kevin Jones. It is an overstable distance driver with a reliable finish. It will hold up on a windy day, and players will be able to see it hold a line for the majority of its flight before that trusty fade kicks in.
952: The Thought Space Athletics Synapse is a high-speed distance driver designed for players with strong arm speeds seeking maximum distance and control. With a stable-to-overstable flight, it offers a slight high-speed turn followed by a reliable fade, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. Notably, the Synapse shares its mold with the Mint Discs Goat, as both are produced by MVP Disc Sports. This connection provides players familiar with the Goat an alternative option with Thought Space Athletics' unique plastic blends and artwork. Available in various premium plastics like Ethos, Aura, and Nebula Ethereal, the Synapse combines durability with aesthetic appeal. It's an excellent choice for advanced players looking to add a dependable bomber to their bag.
958: The Lone Star Discs Warbird is a high-speed, overstable distance driver designed for players seeking a reliable disc that can handle power throws and challenging conditions. With a comfortable rim and predictable flight, it excels in headwinds and is ideal for flex lines and forehand shots. Advanced players will appreciate its dependable fade and torque resistance, while intermediate players can utilize it for controlled distance. The Warbird's design places it between Lone Star's Curl and Bowie drivers, offering a balance of glide and overstability. This makes it versatile for various shot shapes and wind conditions. Available in multiple plastic blends, including Alpha, Bravo, and Glow, the Warbird caters to different preferences for grip and durability. Each plastic type offers unique characteristics, allowing players to select the version that best suits their throwing style and environmental conditions. Overall, the Lone Star Discs Warbird stands out as a dependable distance driver that combines speed, glide, and moderate stability, making it a valuable addition to any disc golfer's bag.
966: The Discmania Splice is the ultra-overstable fairway driver you reach for when your bag needs serious precision. Built to carve sharp hyzers, snappy forehand flare-skips, and dependable roll-outs, it’s a do-it-all utility tool. One user joked it’s “my meat hook” for forced forehand rollers, while another called it a “get out of jail free card” when they needed a scramble shot with serious fade. Brands describe it as 9/3/0/4 territory, but don’t let the numbers fool you—it’s all about control and placement, not max distance. When you want your disc to land right and stay there, the Splice’s got your back.
986: The Lone Star Discs Tumbleweed is a wildly understable distance driver that delivers effortless anhyzers, silky rollers, and tailwind flex shots—without demanding arm power. It’s remarkably easy to grip and glide-friendly, making it a go-to disc for beginners and power hitters alike. One player shared it’s their “only disc I can do full-send rollers with,” while another praised it for achieving big distance even with a noodle arm. In calm or tailwind conditions, the Tumbleweed becomes your personal glider—taming tight woods or carving open fairways with ease. Toss one and watch your shots tumble toward glory.
987: The Lone Star Dos X is a fairway driver designed for control and versatility. Approved by the PDGA in early 2022, it features a comfortable, slightly deeper rim that suits both forehand and backhand grips. Many players describe it as a longer midrange, offering a dependable straight flight with a consistent, mild fade at the end. The stability varies slightly by plastic—Alpha tends to be stable and durable, while Lima is noticeably more understable and beginner-friendly. It’s a solid choice for shaping lines in the woods or for players seeking a go-to driver that doesn’t overpower their form.
989: The Prodigy FX‑3 is a fast, stable fairway driver that debuted in early 2022, designed to bridge the gap between traditional fairways and distance molds. Featuring a slightly wider rim and strong glide, it rides clean hyzer-flips before holding its line and finishing with a crisp fade. Reviewers praise its stability out of the box, describing it as “super controllable” with dependable carry and finish . Its versatile flight is a favorite for both backhand and forehand users, offering more reliability for those stepping up from F-series discs. If you want a precision driver that feels like a fairway with distance chops, the FX‑3 is your go‑to.
990: Thought Space Athletics’ Votum is the brand’s straight-to-stable workhorse fairway, PDGA-approved in March 2021 and designed to bridge the gap between the understable Mantra and the beefy Omen. It handles power cleanly for forward-pushing lines with a confident finish, making it a “point and commit” option for both backhand and forehand. Run chatter matters: Glow versions tend to come out flatter and more overstable, early Ethereal/Ethos and older Aura runs are stable to mildly overstable, and some newer Aura runs (including a popular James Proctor edition) beat in to a touch more turn. In the woods it’s a gap hitter; in wind it stays honest without feeling like a brick—dependable, versatile, and easy to trust.
991: The Animus is a slightly overstable distance driver that bridges the gap between control and power. It’s often described as a more torque-resistant Wraith or a faster Thunderbird . With a comfortable rim and reliable fade, it suits both forehand and backhand throws, offering versatility for players seeking a dependable driver in various conditions.
993: The Thought Space Athletics Omen is the ultimate headwind-fighting champion—a super overstable fairway driver that refuses to roll under pressure. Packed with aggressive fade and no-turn attitude, it's built to smash forehands, hyzer shots, and overhead tosses without mercy. Since its release, it’s gained a reputation as TSA’s beefiest control driver—perfect when you need your disc to land hard and stay put. Some users say it flies akin to a halo Firebird, but thicker and more tank-like right out of the box—with break-in making it just a touch more manageable. When control under pressure matters most, the Omen comes through.
997: The Mint Discs Jackalope is an understable fairway driver built for control and finesse. It excels at hyzer flips, long turnovers, and shaping lines through tight fairways. The rim is shallow and comfortable, giving players of all skill levels a confident grip and smooth release. Whether you're navigating wooded gaps or looking for an easy-turning fairway option, the Jackalope delivers a glidey, reliable flight that holds the angle you give it without fighting to fade out. It’s a favorite for technical setups and creative shot shaping.
1000: The Streamline Jet is an understable distance driver designed for players seeking effortless distance and shot-shaping capabilities. With its high-speed turn and reliable fade, the Jet excels at hyzer flips, long turnovers, and tailwind drives. It's particularly suitable for players with lower arm speeds, offering a straight-to-fade flight path with potential for line shaping. As the understable complement to the Trace, the Jet fills a valuable niche in many players' bags.
1006: The Lone Star Discs Lariat is a stable fairway driver (Speed 9, Glide 5, Turn −1, Fade 1) introduced in late 2023 as a trusted go-to for straight, rope-like flights. Its shallow rim and comfortable grip make it accessible for players across all skill levels. While it won’t dominate windy conditions, it’s prized for its line-holding precision—ideal for hyzer-flips, anhyzer placements, or dead-straight fairway blasts. Reviewers praise its "workhorse" reliability, citing its ability to carve both hyzer and anhyzer shots with ease. A dependable stable disc that feels just right in the hands and delivers on placement.
1012: The Pepper is Clash Discs’ first distance driver, a spicy, overstable disc designed to handle power throws and high winds. With a speed rating of 11, it's ideal for hyzer bombs, headwind shots, and utility throws that require a reliable fade. Its consistent flight path makes it a trustworthy choice in various conditions. Compared to Clash's Spice, the Pepper offers more stability, making it suitable for players with higher arm speeds seeking a dependable finish.
1015: The Clash Discs Ginger was PDGA approved in January 2022 and was one of Clash’s early fairway control drivers. Built for controlled distance, it pushes straight with plenty of high speed integrity and a confident finish. Throwers like it because it is fast enough to stretch a fairway but not so wide rimmed that timing suffers. It handles both forehand and backhand torque from experienced arms yet stays workable for developing players. If your Cookie starts drifting when the wind picks up, reach for a Ginger. It adds spice to your line and finishes with dependable bite.
1016: Ever hear of a disc called the Quarter K? Back in the day, the Quarter K came out with a rounded underside rim, claiming to be the farthest flying disc ever. The claim fell short quickly as disc technology advanced further. The Bohruim is the first disc like the Quarter K since. Its rounded underside rim helps it fly super fast, but maybe isnt the best disc for forehands.
1023: Lone Star’s The Dome is an understable fairway named for Houston’s Astrodome, built to hyzer-flip easily and carve gentle turnovers without scary fade. PDGA-approved on June 6, 2022, it’s beadless with a slight dome and a comfortable, not-too-wide rim that suits developing arms and touch throwers alike. Newer players love it as a first driver for straight stand-ups and tailwind control; seasoned golfers use it as a woods-line shaper, late-turn placement disc, or even a touch roller when powered up. Early runs drew chatter for their gummy feel and easy glide, and it’s been offered in several of Lone Star’s premium blends (including glow) so you can pick the feel you like. Under the Dome, life gets simpler.
1024: The Lone Star Discs Chupacabra burst onto the scene in 2022 as the brand’s ultimate wind warrior fairway driver. It’s ultra-overstable, with a finish that throws a wrench in headwinds and loops those powerful forehands through tight spaces. Compared to Lone Star’s Spur—another nine-speed overstable— the Chupacabra doubles down on fade and torque resistance, making it the go-to when you need extra lockdown. Players appreciate its solid feel and unwavering flight path, calling it “my windproof workhorse.” Whether you’re battling gusts or dialing in a precise hyzer bomb, the Chupacabra brings stability and confidence round after round.
1026: The Yikun Long is a speed 10 driver built for easy distance and shaping lines. It offers a touch of high-speed turn followed by a moderate fade, making it ideal for hyzer flips, long turnovers, and straight shots with finish. It’s well-suited for intermediate arms but can still surprise advanced throwers looking for a finesse option off the tee. The Long flies true to angle and thrives in tailwinds or open-field control shots.
1027: The Yikun Bi is a stable-speed-nine fairway driver approved on December 13, 2021, and quickly became a favorite among Yikun-sponsored players. It offers generous glide with a slight turn before settling into a reliable fade, making it ideal for controlled flex shots and long straight drives. Users praise its moderate rim for comfort and consistent landings, describing it as both predictable and distance-capable. At its core, the Bi fills the slot of a go-to, no-surprise fairway driver—great for backhand tunnel hyzers, forehand control lines, or hyzer-flips that need dependable finishes. A solid workhorse for precision-focused rounds.
1039: The Wild Honey is Clash Discs' accessible, high-speed distance driver designed for effortless glide and gentle turn. It offers a straight-to-understable flight ideal for hyzer flips, long turnovers, and shaping S-curves with minimal effort. Compared to Clash’s Salt, the Wild Honey is more understable and beginner-friendly, making it a great option for players seeking easy distance without sacrificing control. While the Wild Honey is generally understable, some players have reported that certain runs—particularly heavier or more translucent versions—can fly more stable than expected. This variation may be due to differences in run or color, so it's worth noting when selecting a disc. Overall, the Wild Honey is a versatile driver that caters to a wide range of players, offering both accessibility for newer throwers and shot-shaping potential for experienced players.
1040: The Clash Discs Salt is a high-speed distance driver designed for advanced players seeking maximum distance without sacrificing control. With a flight profile featuring a slight high-speed turn and a reliable fade, the Salt excels in delivering long, accurate drives . Crafted in Clash Discs' premium Steady plastic, the Salt offers a durable and flexible feel with excellent grip in various conditions . This makes it a dependable choice for both backhand and forehand throws, capable of handling power throws and performing well in headwinds . With dimensions of 21.4 cm in diameter, 1.7 cm in height, and a rim width of 2.2 cm, the Salt is PDGA approved and caters to players seeking a reliable distance driver . Overall, the Clash Discs Salt stands out as a dependable distance driver that combines speed, glide, and moderate stability, making it a valuable addition to any disc golfer's bag.
1043: The Infinite Discs Dynasty (PDGA-approved January 31, 2022) is a highly versatile, neutral-to-stable fairway driver that offers exceptional straight-line precision. Though it’s rated a speed 9, many players report it flies farther than typical distance drivers, thanks to impressive glide. Its gentle turn is balanced by a firm finish, making it ideal for both controlled hyzer-flips and soft flex lines. Beginners appreciate its ease of use, while advanced throwers value its straight S-curve trajectory that transitions cleanly into reliable fade. Trusted as a go-to control driver, the Dynasty proves that versatility and accuracy can shine together.
1044: You know how the Zen was a signature Essence, and the Midnight Prowl was a signature Origin? The Cloudbreaker was originally a singature DD3, for Eagle McMahon. After a few versions came out and Discmania started producing their own discs, the Cloud Breaker became its own mold seperate from the DD3. Both have the same flight numbers, but the Cloud Breaker is exclusively put out in special runs, most of them end up being Signature Series discs (for either Eagle McMahon or more recently Gannon Buhr). The Cloud Breaker is just like any other DD3 or Destroyer, in that it has copius glide, consistant overstability, and the potential to go very, very, very far.
1045: Kastaplast's overstable 13 speed, the Guld, has some real smash potential just like every disc in box 13-E on the flight guide. Honestly, if you're looking to throw farther than anyone you know, work on throwing any disc in this box (13-E). If you figure any one of them out, you'll smash.
1051: The Innova Power Disc, also known as the Phantom Sword, is a rebranded version of the original Discmania PD (Power Driver). After Discmania transitioned to independent production, Innova retained the rights to the mold and released it under their own branding. Approved by the PDGA on December 27, 2021, the Power Disc is a speed 10, overstable distance driver with moderate glide and a reliable fade. Its designed for power throwers seeking a disc that can handle torque and headwinds, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. The discs stability allows for controlled S-curves and dependable finishes, offering versatility for various shot shapes. Innova later introduced the Power Disc 2, also known as the Elixer, which is based on the Discmania PD2 mold. Approved on April 18, 2022, the Power Disc 2 is a speed 12, overstable distance driver designed for players with significant arm speed, providing a reliable option for long-distance throws in challenging
1052: Innova used to manufacture discs for Discmania. When Discmania split, Innova still had rights to all of their molds, and shorly after they released a slew of them on the Innova Factory Store. Discs like the Mid Disc3 (MD3), Phantom Sword (PD), and this one, the Power Disc2 (PD2). It's the original mold for Discmania's PD2.
1055: The Discmania Tilt isn’t just overstable—it’s in a category of its own. Designed for Simon Lizotte, this disc laughs at headwinds, defies anhyzers, and practically spikes itself. It’s widely considered the most overstable fairway driver on the market by a mile, making it a specialty tool for extreme hyzers, skip shots, forehand flexes, and the occasional trick throw that breaks the laws of physics. Beginners, beware—this thing isn’t here for glide. But if you need something to fade like it’s late for a meeting, the Tilt has your back. Just tilt your expectations accordingly.
1056: The Zenith is MVP’s 11-speed control distance driver, designed in collaboration with 2021 World Champion James Conrad. It offers a balanced flight with moderate glide, slight turn, and a dependable fade, making it ideal for shaping precise lines and handling various conditions. Whether thrown backhand or forehand, the Zenith provides consistent performance, catering to players seeking a reliable driver for controlled distance shots.'
1057: Latitude 64’s Glory is the Royal Line’s trusty overstable fairway—built for wind, forehands, and point-and-dump control when you need a confident finish without jumping to a faster driver. Think “beefier Explorer”: a typically flat top and compact rim give clean releases, strong torque resistance, and predictable ground play for spike hyzers, skip shots, and tight corner placements. It debuted in Royal Grand and has seen standout Grand Orbit team runs—most notably for Silver Lätt—adding a touch of collector shine to a very workmanlike mold. In the lineup it bridges the gap between straight control and true meathooks, delivering dependable fade with just enough forward push to stay versatile.
1058: The Thought Space Athletics Construct is a versatile 10-speed driver that bridges the gap between fairway and distance drivers. With its neutral flight and exceptional glide, it offers a straight trajectory with a gentle fade, making it ideal for players seeking controlled distance. The Construct's design provides a comfortable grip and reliable performance, catering to both backhand and forehand throws. Whether you're powering down for placement shots or pushing for extra distance, the Construct delivers consistent, dependable flights.
1061: The Tombstone is an overstable distance driver named after the signature way this disc will lodge itself into the ground at a spike hyzer angle.
1064: The TeeRex is a fast, overstable distance driver designed for power throwers who need reliable performance in windy conditions. With its high speed and significant fade, its ideal for forehand throws and long hyzer shots. Though out of regular production, the TeeRex occasionally resurfaces in limited runs, remaining a favorite for those seeking a dependable, beefy driver.
1066: The Discmania PD (Power Driver), affectionately known as the Freak, is a speed 10 overstable distance driver that has been a staple in Discmanias lineup since its debut in 2008. Designed for advanced players, the PD offers a reliable flight path with a consistent fade, making it suitable for both backhand and forehand throws. Its versatility allows it to handle various wind conditions and shot shapes, providing confidence and control on the course. Over the years, the PD has seen several iterations, including the 10-Year Anniversary C-Line PD released in 2018, which featured artwork inspired by the original Freak stamp. This special edition was part of a mid-2018 run known for its increased overstability, as noted by Team Discmanias Eagle McMahon, who compared it to the first runs renowned for their reliable fade . The PDs enduring popularity stems from its ability to provide power and control in a single disc, making it a go-to choice for many players seeking a dependable driver that performs consistently across various conditions.
1067: The Athena was the first truly “Paul McBeth” fairway driver from Discraft, and its design clearly nods to the Teebird he relied on throughout his Innova years. It fills the control driver gap between the Undertaker and Anax — neutral enough for straight flights, stable enough for predictability. The Athena’s flight has that classic McBeth feel: laser-line precision with a smooth, late fade. Its release was a subtle statement from Discraft — not just signing McBeth, but replicating the tools that made him dominant. For many players, it’s the modern answer to a seasoned Teebird, reborn in Discraft’s lineup. 1069: Approved on April 24, 2022, the Mint Discs Diamondback is a Speed 9 neutral-to-understable fairway driver that flips easily, floats clean with glide, then finishes the flight with a reliable fade. According to Mint, it's faster than the Alpha and offers more turn than the Grackle, creating a perfect balance between ease and control . Players report it performs comparable to a seasoned Undertaker or a steady Thunderbird, offering forehand-friendly handling and dependable fade even at speed . If you're seeking a versatile fairway driver that’s forgiving yet capable, the Diamondback delivers consistency without compromise.
1074: Cookie was Clash Discs’ first foray into a truly neutral fairway driver — a mold that would showcase Finnish design minimalism with high-end flight balance. Where earlier Clash releases leaned on bold flavors and extreme stabilities, Cookie stood out for restraint. It flies straight with a soft fade, inviting touch and placement rather than muscle. Its release helped solidify Clash as more than a novelty brand, proving they could make timeless, workhorse molds. Among Finnish pros and amateurs alike, the Cookie became the understated disc that quietly does everything well.
1075: The Strike debuted as Birdie’s flagship fairway driver and set the tone for the company’s modern, player-first approach. Designed to handle a wide range of arm speeds, it delivers a clean, straight flight with just enough turn and fade to shape lines without surprises. Its release helped move Birdie beyond its putting roots, showing that their design team could produce tour-caliber drivers too. The Strike feels like a spiritual cousin to discs such as the FD — laser-straight, forgiving, and precise — making it a staple for controlled fairway work.
1078: The Mint Discs Phoenix is a powerhouse overstable control driver and perhaps Mint’s most wind-resistant disc to date. With a hard fade and low glide, it was designed to own headwinds and rough conditions—think spike hyzers and torque-resistant forehands. One Redditor summed it up: “So it's like a less glidey Omen?” And another added: “It is an Omen… 95% sure.” If you're after a dependable disc that punches through gusts, lands with authority, and feels like a grittier Omen alternative, the Phoenix stands ready to rise—just don’t expect it to float on calm days.
1079: The Czar is an overstable speed-11 distance driver designed for players seeking a reliable fade and torque resistance. While it shares identical flight numbers with the Innova Wraith (11/5/-1/3), the Czar is noted for its consistent overstability and dependable finish, making it a trustworthy option for both forehand and backhand throws. Its design offers a comfortable grip and a flight path that maintains stability even in challenging conditions.
1166: The Mermaid was part of Discmania’s now-discontinued Active line, a series designed to offer affordable, beginner-friendly molds made overseas. True to its name, the Mermaid’s defining feature is that it floats in water , making it a favorite for courses with lakes and ponds in play. Flight-wise, it’s a straight, neutral fairway driver that’s easy to control and forgiving for developing arms. It doesn’t take much power to get full flight, and its soft fade at the end keeps it from diving too soon. Though the Active line has sunsetted, the Mermaid remains a cult favorite for anyone tired of donating plastic to the drink.
1168: The DD1 is Discmania’s answer to a controllable distance driver—think of it as a more user-friendly DD3. With a narrower rim and straighter flight, it offers high glide and a reliable fade, making it ideal for shaping lines in the woods or open field shots. If the DD3 feels like too much disc, the DD1 might be just right.
1169: The Yeet is Hooligan Discs’ flagship overstable distance driver, designed for players seeking a reliable disc that can handle power throws and challenging conditions. With a comfortable rim and predictable flight, it excels in headwinds and is ideal for flex lines and forehand shots. Advanced players will appreciate its dependable fade and torque resistance, while intermediate players can utilize it for controlled distance. Initially produced in collaboration with Lone Star Discs, the Yeet is now manufactured by Gateway Disc Sports, ensuring consistent quality and performance. Available in premium plastics like Alpha and Bravo, the Yeet offers excellent grip and durability, making it a versatile addition to any disc golfer's bag.
1171: The Hooligan Discs Thread is a neutral-to-understable fairway/control driver approved in July 2022 (retooled April 2024), designed for smooth hyzer-flips, long straight flights, and controlled rollers. With a moderate dome and comfortable rim, it releases cleanly—even for developing arms—and offers dependable glide before gently fading. It fills a gap in Hooligan’s lineup for approachable yet shot-shapable fairway work, making it a favorite for backhand tunnel shots and forehand finesse lines. Advanced players also tap into its roller potential for strategic placement. If you want a versatile, finger-friendly workhorse that rewards clean form and shot making, the Thread delivers.
1172: The Hooligan Discs Vibe is a versatile distance driver offering a controllable, glidey flight. It excels at hyzer flips and long turnovers, making it suitable for players seeking easy distance with manageable stability. The Vibe's comfortable rim and consistent flight path make it a reliable choice for various shot shapes and conditions.
1180: The Nimitz is Lone Star’s stable-to-overstable distance driver, designed to slot between the Curl and Warbird in their lineup. With a flight path that offers a touch of high-speed turn followed by a reliable fade, it’s a versatile option for players seeking controlled distance.
